definition: A cap or target on how many tokens a reasoning model may spend thinking before answering, used both as a measurement device (OAA_t scores accuracy only under a given token threshold t) and as a control target for training methods that calibrate output length to problem difficulty (as in the archive's overthinking-mitigation literature more broadly).

evidence.note: Introduces OptimalThinkingBench, a unified benchmark pairing OverthinkingBench (simple queries) and UnderthinkingBench (hard reasoning/math) with a shared F1 metric, showing that none of 33 evaluated LLMs balances accuracy and thinking-token efficiency.
evidence.title: OptimalThinkingBench: Evaluating Over and Underthinking in LLMs

name: thinking-token budget
